Powering Performance Marketplaces in Digital Media

QuinStreet is a pioneer in powering decentralized online  marketplaces that match searchers and “research and compare” consumers with brands
. We run these virtual- and private-label marketplaces in one of the nation’s largest media networks.
Our industry leading segmentation and AI-driven  matching technologies help consumers find better solutions and brands faster.
 They allow brands to target and reach in-market customer prospects with pinpoint segment-by-segment accuracy, and to pay only for performance results.
Our campaign-results-driven matching decision engines and optimization algorithms are built from over 20 years and billions of dollars of online media experience.
We believe in:
The direct measurability of digital media.
Performance marketing. (We pioneered it.)
The advantages of technology.

We bring all this together to deliver truly great results for consumers and brands in the world’s biggest channel.

Job Category

As a key member of the Strategic Marketing & Analytics team, you will be responsible for data-driven insights that enable QuinStreets Marketing and Media teams to maximize profitability while developing customer relationships. You will gather, organize, and aggregate complex sets of data in order to produce meaningful business insight in areas such as ad network optimization, ad merchandising, marketing performance, quality monitoring, partner development, product testing, and more. You will also communicate your insights and findings to various members of our Client, Media, Analytics, and Executive teams.

Responsibilities

Work closely with media and client managers to understand business opportunities for media, client and market growth.
Actively mine data to develop actionable insights from our proprietary datasets using various statistical techniques.
Evaluate strategies and forecast their expected impact to the key performance indicators.
Support analysis and monitoring of business metrics and trends.
Key liaison between business and technical teams in managing day to day data analytics.
Lead a small team of analysts, setting longer-term goals and ensuring short-term operational efficiency.

Requirements

Record of high academic achievement with a BS degree in Business, Economics, Engineering, Math/Science, or otherwise proven background in business/analytics. MS preferred, Bonus points for statistics.
8+ years of work experience in data analytics/science.
Strong understanding of statistical methods used in to elicit insights from data.
Strong analytical mindset with a drive toward actionable insights from data.
Deep interest in online marketing and media industry. Industry experience a plus.
High internal motivation with ability to understand the full stack of product development.
Willingness to initiate and own research, exploration, and analysis from start to finish for any business problem.
Good interpersonal skills and ability to remain focused-yet-flexible in a fast-paced internet company environment.
Proficiency in MS Excel, Tableau and SQL.
Familiarity with Python (preferred) or R programming to the level necessary to perform ad-hoc analysis.
Experience managing a small team

Job Description

The Data Analyst 3 will be a senior member of the Supply Chain Intelligence (SCI) team, owning the delivery of data and insights for Nordstrom's Distribution Center and warehouse operations. The Data Analyst 3 will provide ongoing data support, performance analysis, and storytelling, which will lead to value creation and enable the next cycle of growth within Nordstrom — supporting reliable, accurate reporting and data pipeline integrity across inbound, outbound, inventory, and labor operations to help DCs run efficiently and serve customers and stores across the Nordstrom businesses.

A day in the life…

Operate as an insight partner to Distribution Center and Supply Chain leadership, not just a data provider — translating reliable, well-governed data into diagnosis, root cause, and recommended action
Own "the truth" and governance in data and process including the intake, management, automation, and integrity of data sourced from warehouse management systems and downstream data pipelines, so reporting rests on stable, validated data rather than repeated ad hoc extraction from source systems
Champion the data needs and priorities of the SCI team, coordinating with key data/business partners across the Nordstrom organization including DC Operations, Nordstrom Technology, Finance, and Supply Chain leadership
Lead and support data design requirements and delivery for SCI reporting programs and initiatives, including an ongoing legacy-to-modern BI platform migration and a broader shift toward more centralized, self-service analytics
Partner with data engineering to help ensure upstream data is accurate and well-defined, so downstream reporting can rely on consistent logic instead of every analyst re-deriving it independently
Conduct regular audits to ensure data integrity and compliance; monitor and help troubleshoot data pipeline issues, escalating and resolving in partnership with engineering
Shift time from data validation toward analysis: use a more reliable data foundation to prioritize hypothesis testing, trend diagnosis, and forward-looking recommendations over one-off data pulls
Support DC and Supply Chain business partners in the development of modernized reporting and effective analysis, creating compelling narratives and storytelling through data
Support the analysis and diagnosis of end-to-end DC and warehouse performance and provide actionable guidance to improve results
Identify and develop new measures and KPIs that support the continuous improvement and optimization of Nordstrom's supply chain
Collaborate with supply chain and operations teams to identify signals and visibility needed to enhance operations and controls; build reporting to support control monitoring
Leverage AI-assisted tools such as Claude Code and Claude Desktop to accelerate exploratory analysis and SCI reporting workflows, further shifting analyst time from manual data wrangling to insight generation

You own this if you have…

Degree in Finance, Statistics, Mathematics, Analytics, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field required (Masters preferred)
5+ years of data management and data analysis; demonstrated ability to technically mentor and support the development of junior analysts
Demonstrated ability to move beyond descriptive reporting to diagnostic and prescriptive analysis — identifying root cause and recommending action, not just surfacing metrics
Strong understanding of ETL processes, data management principles, and data pipeline development using Apache Airflow, Dataflow
Strong understanding of normalized and de-normalized data, data warehousing, query construction, and dimensional data modeling, with applied skills in SQL and hands-on experience with BigQuery
Experience extracting and manipulating large datasets from relational databases (e.g., Oracle, PostgreSQL, or MySQL)
Proficiency in data querying and visualization/reporting tools (e.g., Tableau, Looker, IBM Cognos)
Advanced knowledge of version control tools (gitlab/github)
Experience with AI-assisted development and productivity tools (e.g., Claude Code, Claude Desktop) to accelerate analysis, automate data workflows, and Looker development preferred
Strong operational business understanding, including potential impact of business decisions on various internal/external stakeholders and systems
Supply chain expertise in retail or consumer goods preferred, with specific focus on warehouse operations, distribution, fulfillment, receiving, or inventory management, and understanding of industry dynamics

Brief Job Description

This position is open to U.S. Citizens and permanent residents.

This onsite role requires the selected candidate to work from an HHS office in Austin, Texas.

The Program Specialist V, Project Coordinator provides foundational portfolio and project coordination, oversight documentation, reporting, and compliance support within the IT Customer Experience & Delivery organization, ensuring IT initiatives are managed with high visibility, predictability, quality, and alignment to business goals. The position supports the planning, development, editing, quality assurance, and approval routing of executive-ready oversight deliverables required for project approval and state/federal financial participation and drives timely resolution of questions and issues raised during review cycles. The role serves as an advisor to IT project managers and cross-functional IT enablement partners by translating state/federal oversight expectations into actionable guidance, and by supporting effective project controls, performance monitoring, and risk/issue escalation to strengthen project outcomes across assigned portfolios.

The Project Coordinator supports accurate and consistent project health and performance reporting, including the production of clear executive-level status narratives and the continuous improvement of data quality and portfolio analytics used for decision-making. The position coordinates compliance activities and communications with the State’s Quality Assurance Team (QAT) using the DIR project delivery framework, supports required reporting submissions (including monitoring and quarterly reporting). This role contributes to targeted training and outreach—supported by job aids and tool-focused guidance—to improve stakeholder understanding of oversight requirements, timelines, and quality standards, while improving repeatable processes and technology-enabled solutions that increase efficiency and strengthen governance.

Essential Job Functions (EJFs)

Attends work on a regular and predictable schedule in accordance with agency policy and performs other duties as assigned.

Documentation Development, Quality Control, and Approval Routing (25%)

Supports the end-to-end coordination, development, and submission of project oversight documentation required to obtain and maintain project approval and financial participation from state and federal oversight authorities. This includes gathering and validating input from project teams and stakeholders, drafting/editing documents for completeness, accuracy, and clarity, coordinating internal quality review, routing for approvals, monitoring review status, and supporting the resolution of comments and issues. Reviews documentation packages for quality and submits within required timeframes, while maintaining organized records that support audit readiness, traceability, and continuity across the project lifecycle.

Compliance Reporting and Coordination (20%)

Coordinates with the State’s Quality Assurance Team (QAT) to support compliance with required QAT reporting standards. Participates in discussions with QAT, coordinates responses to questions/issues, ensures required reporting packages are accurate and defensible, and enters project performance information into the SPAR system with attention to detail. Works cross-functionally with project managers, governance partners, and portfolio stakeholders to ensure external reporting aligns to internal project status, and that compliance obligations are met while protecting the agency.

Portfolio Monitoring, Controls Support, and Risk/Issue Escalation (20%)

Performs portfolio-level monitoring of project performance, quality, and risk to promote high-performing projects and predictable delivery outcomes. Reviews project status updates for quality and risk signals, identifies trends or emerging issues, and proactively escalates risks/issues to PMO leadership and appropriate governance channels. Supports project control activities across key lifecycle moments (initiation, corrective actions such as “go-to-green,” changes, and closure) by coordinating required artifacts, recommending corrective actions, and tracking follow-through. Contributes to project performance & reporting functions in governance and cross-coordination forums to ensure risks, decisions, and commitments are visible, documented, and actioned.

Performance Reporting, Data Quality Assurance, and Toolset Subject Matter Expertise (20%)

Ensures project and portfolio reporting is produced efficiently, accurately, and consistently across the assigned portfolio(s). Supports data-quality practices within the project/portfolio management system by performing routine portfolio analysis, validating project health reporting, and influencing project managers to maintain high-quality data through regular engagement. Develops and maintains subject matter expertise in project management toolsets (e.g., PPM, dashboards and reporting platforms such as Power BI, document approval/routing tools, and other emerging technologies) to strengthen reporting reliability and stakeholder transparency. Produces portfolio performance summaries and visualizations that enable leadership decision-making and create consistent understanding of portfolio status.

Project Management Support Services, Proposal/Intake Pipeline Support, and Continuous Improvement (15%)

Provides front-line project performance and coordination services for assigned portfolios by triaging, analyzing, resolving, and responding to project management support requests, and by liaising with IT enablement partners (CTO, BRM, CISO, Application Development, Infrastructure Services, etc.) to influence sound decisions and remove blockers. Supports the coordination, scoping, analysis, and estimation of new IT proposals that form the future project pipeline. Facilitates and documents meetings by capturing notes, action items, and decisions and publishing outcomes to stakeholders. Participates in process improvement initiatives that enhance operational efficiency, strengthen governance, and leverage automation/AI-enabled solutions where appropriate. Develops and delivers targeted training, job aids, and outreach sessions to project managers and cross-functional IT stakeholders to reinforce oversight expectations, reporting timelines, data-quality standards, and QAT/SPAR compliance requirements across assigned portfolios.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities (KSAs)

Knowledge of applicable federal and state laws, rules, policies, and procedures related to IT project oversight and compliance.
Knowledge of portfolio, project, and governance standards, controls, and escalation processes.
Knowledge of project management lifecycles and DIR project delivery framework requirements, including QAT oversight.

Ability to work independently while exercising sound judgment and professionalism.
Ability to support continuous improvement by standardizing workflows and leveraging technology-enabled solutions.

Registrations, Licensure Requirements Or Certifications

Initial Screening Criteria

This includes gathering and validating input from project teams and stakeholders, drafting/editing documents for completeness, accuracy, and clarity, coordinating internal quality review, routing for approvals, monitoring review status, and supporting the resolution of comments and issues. Reviews documentation packages for quality and submits within required timeframes, while maintaining organized records that support audit readiness, traceability, and continuity across the project lifecycle.

Compliance Reporting and Coordination (20%)

Coordinates with the State’s Quality Assurance Team (QAT) to support compliance with required QAT reporting standards. Participates in discussions with QAT, coordinates responses to questions/issues, ensures required reporting packages are accurate and defensible, and enters project performance information into the SPAR system with attention to detail. Works cross-functionally with project managers, governance partners, and portfolio stakeholders to ensure external reporting aligns to internal project status, and that compliance obligations are met while protecting the agency.

Portfolio Monitoring, Controls Support, and Risk/Issue Escalation (20%)

Performs portfolio-level monitoring of project performance, quality, and risk to promote high-performing projects and predictable delivery outcomes. Reviews project status updates for quality and risk signals, identifies trends or emerging issues, and proactively escalates risks/issues to PMO leadership and appropriate governance channels. Supports project control activities across key lifecycle moments (initiation, corrective actions such as “go-to-green,” changes, and closure) by coordinating required artifacts, recommending corrective actions, and tracking follow-through. Contributes to project performance & reporting functions in governance and cross-coordination forums to ensure risks, decisions, and commitments are visible, documented, and actioned.

Performance Reporting, Data Quality Assurance, and Toolset Subject Matter Expertise (20%)

Ensures project and portfolio reporting is produced efficiently, accurately, and consistently across the assigned portfolio(s). Supports data-quality practices within the project/portfolio management system by performing routine portfolio analysis, validating project health reporting, and influencing project managers to maintain high-quality data through regular engagement. Develops and maintains subject matter expertise in project management toolsets (e.g., PPM, dashboards and reporting platforms such as Power BI, document approval/routing tools, and other emerging technologies) to strengthen reporting reliability and stakeholder transparency. Produces portfolio performance summaries and visualizations that enable leadership decision-making and create consistent understanding of portfolio status.

Project Management Support Services, Proposal/Intake Pipeline Support, and Continuous Improvement (15%)

Provides front-line project performance and coordination services for assigned portfolios by triaging, analyzing, resolving, and responding to project management support requests, and by liaising with IT enablement partners (CTO, BRM, CISO, Application Development, Infrastructure Services, etc.) to influence sound decisions and remove blockers. Supports the coordination, scoping, analysis, and estimation of new IT proposals that form the future project pipeline. Facilitates and documents meetings by capturing notes, action items, and decisions and publishing outcomes to stakeholders. Participates in process improvement initiatives that enhance operational efficiency, strengthen governance, and leverage automation/AI-enabled solutions where appropriate. Develops and delivers targeted training, job aids, and outreach sessions to project managers and cross-functional IT stakeholders to reinforce oversight expectations, reporting timelines, data-quality standards, and QAT/SPAR compliance requirements across assigned portfolios.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities (KSAs)

Knowledge of applicable federal and state laws, rules, policies, and procedures related to IT project oversight and compliance.
Knowledge of portfolio, project, and governance standards, controls, and escalation processes.
Knowledge of project management lifecycles and DIR project delivery framework requirements, including QAT oversight.
Knowledge of performance monitoring, risk/issue management, and quality assurance methodologies.
Skill in coordination and preparation of required project oversight and compliance deliverables.

Ability to interpret and apply oversight guidance to ensure compliance and audit readiness.
Ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines in a structured oversight environment.
Ability to communicate effectively with leadership, project teams, and oversight partners.
Ability to work independently while exercising sound judgment and professionalism.
Ability to support continuous improvement by standardizing workflows and leveraging technology-enabled solutions.

Registrations, Licensure Requirements Or Certifications

Project Management Professional (PMP) and/or Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM) is preferred. Certified Texas Contract Manager (CTCM) is preferred.

Initial Screening Criteria

Degree from a 4-year university is preferred. Bachelor’s degree in business administration, technology, healthcare, or related field OR equivalent combination of education and directly related experience on a year-for-year basis.
Experience in writing, editing, and presenting project deliverables / documents for an executive level audience in a large company or organization.

new_jobs.title: JCamp 180 Program Coordinator
new_jobs.description:
Description

Reporting to the Director of JCamp 180, the Program Coordinator provides project management and administrative support to a dynamic team that delivers grants, professional development, and organizational consulting services to nonprofit Jewish summer camps across North America.

This role supports a team of consultants, the Senior Program Manager, and the Director by coordinating projects, managing logistics, maintaining systems, and ensuring programs and services are delivered on time, within budget, and with a high level of quality. The position requires exceptional organization, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a collaborative environment.

Team members work from the Foundation's headquarters in Agawam, Massachusetts, the New York City office, and remote locations throughout the United States and Canada. The team gathers several times each year for an annual retreat, the JCamp 180 Conference, and Foundation-wide meetings and events.

Requirements

Responsibilities

Working closely with colleagues across the Foundation, the Program Coordinator ensures JCamp 180's programs, grants, and consulting services are delivered with excellence, supporting nonprofit Jewish summer camps in building stronger organizations and vibrant communities.

Professional Development Program Support (30%)

Provide project management and logistical support for JCamp 180's online and in-person professional development programs.

Manage project timelines, recurring meetings, and the annual application process, including application materials, interview scheduling, and coordination with program leads.
Coordinate logistics for in-person and virtual programs, including venues, vendors, contracts, travel, catering, transportation, and Zoom support.
Monitor program budgets, process vendor invoices, and track expenses throughout the year.
Develop and distribute participant communications, maintain current program information on the JCamp 180 website, and ensure consistent branding and best practices across all professional development programs.
Coordinate participant evaluations and prepare summary reports to measure program effectiveness.

Department Operations (30%)

Provide administrative, logistical, and operational support to the JCamp 180 team.

Coordinate the biannual renewal process for affiliated camps and support consultant recruitment efforts.
Support consultants with meeting coordination, presentation development, note-taking, research, and tracking project deliverables.
Schedule team meetings, retreats, and gatherings, coordinating logistics such as venues, catering, speakers, and materials.
Maintain Salesforce data, generate reports, support staff in using the system effectively, and assist with testing and implementing new functionality.
Maintain the team's SharePoint site and organize department documentation and annual planning materials.
Process invoices and ensure timely payment of department expenses.
Support special projects, including research, resource development, template creation, and content development to strengthen JCamp 180's consulting practice.
Assist with Foundation-wide events and initiatives as needed, including conference support, video projects, and management of JCamp 180-branded materials and inventory.

JCamp 180 Conference (20%)

Provide project management and logistical support for JCamp 180's annual conference.

Coordinate presenter contracts, honoraria, invoices, and vendor documentation.
Partner with the Conference & Events team to manage venue logistics, accommodations, catering, audiovisual needs, and conference operations.
Manage conference communications, provide logistical support for speakers and presenters, and assist with on-site event execution.
Coordinate post-conference evaluations and documentation and prepare briefing materials and scheduling support for the Director.

Grant Administration & Support (20%)

Support the implementation and administration of JCamp 180 grant programs.

Partner with the Grants Department to support grant implementation, reporting, deadlines, and project management.
Assist in developing grant guidelines, application materials, and supporting documentation.
Collaborate with the Marketing & Communications team to promote grant opportunities and prepare grant progress reports.
Compile and analyze qualitative and quantitative data for reports and presentations.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate is a highly organized project manager who enjoys building systems, coordinating complex initiatives, and supporting a collaborative team. They are passionate about helping nonprofit organizations thrive and advancing JCamp 180's mission to strengthen Jewish summer camps and the communities they serve. Candidates who bring a strong connection to Jewish camping and enthusiasm for supporting its long-term success are especially encouraged to apply.

Excellent organizational skills and exceptional attention to detail.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with a team.
Demonstrated project management abilities.
Ability to improve processes and develop efficient internal systems.
Curiosity about organizational development, evaluation, nonprofit consulting, and philanthropy.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Experience using collaboration and project management tools such as Zoom, SharePoint, Asana, Mailchimp, Airtable, Jotform, SurveyMonkey, Bizzabo, Slack, and Mentimeter.
Familiarity with Salesforce or similar CRM platforms, along with the ability to quickly learn new technologies.
Creative problem-solving skills and a willingness to contribute ideas in a collaborative environment.
Flexibility to support evolving team priorities and special projects.
Ability to travel occasionally (approximately three to five trips per year).

Preferred Qualifications

Passion for the mission of the Harold Grinspoon Foundation and JCamp 180.
Knowledge of or experience with Jewish camping, the Jewish communal sector, or nonprofit organizations.
Bachelor's degree in nonprofit management, communications, project management, Jewish communal service, or a related field.

Physical Requirements

Prolonged periods of sitting while working on a computer.
Ability to occasionally lift and move up to 15 pounds.

Location

This role is hybrid from our New York City office. Hybrid employees are expected onsite 60% of the time.

Compensation

A competitive hourly rate of $31.25–$37.26 per hour, commensurate with experience (equivalent to an annualized salary of $65,000–$77,500 based on full-time employment of 40 hours per week).

new_jobs.description:
WebMD Health Services is part of the WebMD family. We have been designing well-being programs for employers and health plans for over 20 years. Our mission is to empower organizations and their populations to improve well-being through personalized, strategic partnerships.

Overview:

WebMD Health Services (WHS) is a division of WebMD whose mission is to provide expert guidance that inspires people to take charge of their health. We do this by helping people understand their health risks, make smart health care decisions, and take active steps toward living healthier lives. Our health, wellness and transparency services power programs from employers, health plans and government organizations are delivered online, onsite, and telephonically. Learn more at webmdhealthservices.com.
WebMD is an Equal Opportunity Employer of Minorities, Females, Protected Veterans, and Individuals with Disabilities.

Position Description:

The Well-being Program Coordinator will work collaboratively with the designated client’s health promotion team to deliver well-being programming and face-to-face health coaching to eligible participants as well as help to raise awareness of the onsite program and the WebMD products and services that enable it.

The Program Coordinator is responsible for client satisfaction, retention, and reference-ability. S/he will act as a customer advocate, as well as a point of contact with senior customer stakeholders to increase participant engagement and maximize value delivered through the WebMD relationship. They can provide thought leadership and support program planning and impact assessment, as well as coordination and promotion of service.

Program Coordinator’s proactively identify opportunities for service delivery enhancement and improvement. As opportunities are identified, they work with other Client Success staff, Account and Product Management, to improve processes, and develop new solutions.

This role includes:
Program Leadership

Lead the planning and execution of onsite wellness initiatives and annual engagement strategies.
Develop creative campaigns that increase awareness and participation.
Coordinate health screenings, challenges, educational sessions, and special events.

Health Coaching & Biometric Screenings

Provide one-on-one, virtual, and group health coaching.
Use motivational interviewing to support sustainable behavior change.
Conduct biometric screenings, blood pressure checks, and vision screenings.

Client Partnership

Build trusted relationships with HR, Benefits, UAW, and site leadership.
Serve as a wellness advisor by identifying opportunities to improve engagement and program outcomes.
Build and support the Well-being Champion Network.

Project & Data Management

Manage multiple projects simultaneously while meeting deadlines.
Track participation, analyze trends, and provide recommendations.
Maintain accurate documentation and reporting.

What Success Looks Like

Increased employee engagement in wellness programs.
Strong partnerships with client stakeholders.
High-quality coaching experiences.
Well-executed events delivered on time.
Continuous improvement driven by participant feedback and data.

As a member of WebMD Health Services, you may have access to confidential and sensitive information (including Protected Health Information) that will require you to follow additional protocols to ensure the security of our data. As a core requirement, you must implement and act in accordance with the organization’s information security policies; protect assets from unauthorized access, disclosure, modification, destruction, or interference; execute security processes or activities; and report security events or potential events or other security risks to the appropriate parties within the organization.

Qualifications, skills and experience:

Required:

Minimum of a bachelor's degree required in a health-related field
2 years Wellness Coordinator/Health Coaching or similar health and wellness client-facing experience
Ability to work independently onsite at client location and manage multiple competing priorities
Experience and comfort using Microsoft and Google office products
Excellent organizational and time management skills
Flexibility to occasionally support early morning, evening, or special event programming, as well as periodic travel to other client locations

Ideal Candidates:

Excellent communication/people skills, including proven ability to adapt to individual communication styles and client work groups, including office and manufacturing environments
Solutions-oriented and independent problem-solving mindset
Willing and able to occasionally travel out of the state to support client or WebMD
Experience analyzing and interpreting data
Demonstrated enthusiasm for interacting with participants
Thrive in dynamic, fast-paced settings
Proficient with various types of technology and be able to accurately enter data into databases, spreadsheets, and other systems

Preferred:

CHES or Certified Health Coach
Experience conducting fingerstick TC/HDL/GLU screenings, blood pressure measurement, and results coaching
Experience and comfort delivering health presentations/programming and interacting with participants both in-person and virtually
Experience utilizing Canva Pro
Experience delivering presentations to small and large groups

Compensation:
$ 41,000 - $43,000

Benefits:
Employees in this position are eligible to participate in the company sponsored benefit programs, including the following within the first 12 months of employment:
Health Insurance (medical, dental, and vision coverage)
Paid Time Off (including vacation, sick leave, and flexible holiday days)
401(k) Retirement Plan with employer matching
Life and Disability Insurance
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
Commuter and/or Transit Benefits (if applicable)

Eligibility for specific benefits may vary based on job classification, schedule (e.g., full-time vs. part-time), work location and length of employment.
